cards: Clovis I was king of the Franks in the late fifth and early sixth centuries and founder of the Merovingian dynasty.
Augustine of Hippo was a Christian theologian and bishop from Roman North Africa, born at Thagaste in Numidia.
Attila was ruler of the Huns from 434, at first jointly with his brother Bleda, and sole ruler from about 445 until his death in 453.
Childeric I was a king of the Salian Franks, traditionally the son of Merovech, who ruled from Tournai until his death around 481.
Cunedda is a figure of Welsh tradition said to have come with his sons from Manaw Gododdin, near the head of the Firth of Forth, in the 5th century to drive the Irish from north Wales.
Kalidasa was a classical Sanskrit poet and dramatist, widely regarded as the greatest writer in the language.
Flavius Aetius was the leading general of the Western Roman Empire for some twenty years under Valentinian III.
Emperor Wu of Liu Song, born Liu Yu, was a general of humble origins who rose to dominate the Eastern Jin court.
Honorius was Roman emperor in the West from 395 CE, the son of Theodosius I.
Jangsu was king of Goguryeo from 413 to 491, one of the longest reigns in Korean history.
Tao Yuanming, also called Tao Qian, was a Chinese poet of the Eastern Jin and early Liu Song periods.
Vortigern was a 5th-century British ruler who, according to Gildas, Bede and the Historia Brittonum, invited Saxon mercenaries under Hengist and Horsa to defend Britain, only for them to rebel and…
Aryabhata was an Indian mathematician and astronomer of the late 5th century CE.
late 5th century CE · South & Southeast Asia
Chandragupta II, also called Vikramaditya, was a ruler of the Gupta Empire who reigned from about 375 to 415 CE.
Faxian was a Chinese Buddhist monk who travelled to India in search of Buddhist texts, staying there during 399–414 CE.
399–414 CE in India · South & Southeast Asia
Priscus of Panium was an Eastern Roman diplomat and historian of the 5th century.
Alaric II was king of the Visigoths from 484 to 507, ruling much of Gaul and Hispania from Toulouse.
Euric was king of the Visigoths from 466 to 484, having taken the throne by murdering his brother Theodoric II.
Peroz I was a Sasanian king of Persia who reigned from 459 to 484.
Rechila was king of the Suebi in Gallaecia from 438 to 448.
Yazdegerd II was king of the Sasanian Empire of Persia from 438 to 457.
Gunderic was king of the Hasding Vandals from about 407 to 428.
The Lady of Cao is the name given to a Moche woman of high rank whose richly furnished tomb was found in 2006 at Huaca Cao Viejo, part of the El Brujo complex on the north coast of Peru.
Mesrop Mashtots was an Armenian monk and scholar who created the Armenian alphabet around 405 with the support of King Vramshapuh and the Catholicos Sahak.
Rechiar was king of the Suebi from 448 to 456, the first Germanic king known to have been a Catholic and the first to mint coins in his own name.
Saint Remigius (c. 437–533) was bishop of Reims for more than seventy years.
Theodosius II was emperor of the Eastern Roman Empire from 408 to 450, succeeding his father Arcadius as a child.
Alaric I was a king of the Visigoths who led his people in conflicts with the Roman Empire in the late fourth and early fifth centuries.
Flavius Ardabur Aspar was an Eastern Roman general of Alan descent who dominated the court at Constantinople for much of the mid-fifth century.
Orosius, or Paulus Orosius, was a Christian priest and historian from Roman Hispania and a pupil of Augustine of Hippo.
Purnavarman was a king of Tarumanagara, the earliest known Hindu kingdom of western Java, who ruled in the fifth century CE.
Sidonius Apollinaris was a Gallo-Roman aristocrat, poet and bishop of Clermont from about 470.
Skandagupta was an emperor of the Gupta Empire who reigned c. 455–467 CE.
Ambrosius Aurelianus was a Romano-British war leader of the 5th century who, according to Gildas, rallied the Britons against the Anglo-Saxon invaders after the end of Roman rule.
K'inich Yax K'uk' Mo' was the founder of the royal dynasty of Copán, in present-day Honduras, who took power in 426 CE.
Wallia was king of the Visigoths from 415 to 418.
Xiao Baojuan was emperor of the Southern Qi dynasty from 498 to 501, posthumously demoted to Marquess of Donghun.
Xiao Daocheng was a general who became the power behind the Liu Song throne in southern China.
Zeno was Eastern Roman emperor from 474 to 491, with a break in 475–476 when he was driven out by the usurper Basiliscus.
Anastasius I was emperor of the Eastern Roman Empire from 491 to 518.
